title: The Choir of the Undercroft
premise: Coral Lockridge takes a teaching post at Marrowgate Academy, where students vanish one desk at a time and the staff's cheerful denial feels rehearsed. His habit of recording everything — attendance logs, tape dictations, even his own sleep — becomes both shield and summons when the tapes begin capturing a second voice beneath his own, answering questions he never asked aloud. The voice belongs to the Undercroft Choir, a congregation of the taken who sing a verse that rewrites whoever hears it whole. To save the last missing student and himself, Coral must descend into the flooded well beneath the school, learn the song's final verse by ear without ever singing along, and break the cycle before the well refills — an ending that costs him his recorded self but returns the children, changed and unremembering, to their desks.
about_author: Beatrix Nakamura is the pen name of a former school archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing institutional records before turning to horror. She writes in longhand near water and claims her best ideas arrive as dictation she doesn't remember making.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: POV Coral. He arrives at Marrowgate Academy on a rain-gray morning, meets Headmistress Vane, and notices a classroom photo where one child's face has been carefully inked out. Emotional beat: wary optimism curdling into unease.

chapters.title: The Missing-Class Problem
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A student, Imogen Pell, is absent; staff call it 'a family matter' with identical phrasing. Coral begins his documentation ritual — carbon copies of everything. Beat: the comfort of record-keeping as control.

chapters.title: Carbon and Prayer
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Flashback to Coral's childhood stammer and how writing things down made them real and therefore survivable. He tapes his first dictation log. Beat: establishing documentation as devotion.

chapters.title: Desk Thirty-One
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Imogen's desk sits empty but warm each morning. Another student, Tobias, whispers that the school 'sings you down' if you stop belonging. Beat: first crack in institutional normalcy.

chapters.title: Vane's Warmth
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Headmistress Vane hosts a welcoming tea; every colleague repeats the same anecdotes word-for-word. Coral notices the faculty photograph has more inked-out faces than students. Beat: dread dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: First Recording
chapters.summary: POV Coral. He records the evening sounds of the dormitory wing for his log and captures a low harmonic under the boiler room that no pipe should make. Beat: curiosity overriding caution.

chapters.title: The Sleep Tapes
chapters.summary: POV Coral. He begins taping his own sleep to monitor his stammer. Playback reveals him talking — fluently — in a voice not quite his. Beat: violation of the self.

chapters.title: Questions Answered
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The second voice answers questions Coral never asked: 'Where is Imogen?' — 'Down.' He plays the tape for Tobias, who goes white and transfers schools within hours. Beat: isolation deepening.

chapters.title: Undercroft Door
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Following the harmonic, Coral finds a door behind the boiler room marked CHOIR PRACTICE — SEALED 1974. It is warm. Beat: threshold terror.

chapters.title: The Inked Faces
chapters.summary: POV Coral. He matches the inked-out photo faces to names in pre-1974 registers: all vanished mid-term, all logged as 'family matters' in Vane's own hand, decades apart. Beat: the horror of pattern.

chapters.title: Second Verse, First Hearing
chapters.summary: POV Coral. In sleep, Coral hums two bars he's never heard. His roommate's goldfish dies overnight; the water smells of well-water. Beat: contamination.

chapters.title: Tobias's Letter
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A letter arrives from Tobias: 'Don't learn it. They teach you while you sleep. I can hear it now and I never went down there.' Beat: guilt and urgency.

chapters.title: Imogen's Notebook
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral finds Imogen's hidden notebook in the library stacks — pages of transcribed lyrics, the final verse torn out. Margin note: 'It only needs one voice to finish it.' Beat: hope weaponized.

chapters.title: Faculty Meeting
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral confronts Vane privately; she admits the school was built over a drowned chapel congregation and that 'the well refills every generation.' She offers him tenure. Beat: corruption of power offered gently.

chapters.title: Tenure and Teeth
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral signs nothing but pretends to consider it, buying access to the sealed archives. Vane's smile doesn't reach her eyes anymore — or perhaps it never did. Beat: complicity as survival.

chapters.title: The 1974 Register
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The archive yields the choir's origin: a chapel congregation sealed alive below during renovations, singing until the water rose. Their song became a lure. Beat: tragic history revealed.

chapters.title: Hum in the Walls
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The harmonic spreads through the school; students hum in unison during exams without realizing. Coral wears wax in his ears and documents his own resistance. Beat: siege mentality.

chapters.title: Third Voice
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The sleep tapes now hold three voices: his, the choir's, and a child's — Imogen, singing from below, asking Coral by name to come down. Beat: personal stakes ignite.

chapters.title: What Documentation Can't Hold
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral discovers pages of his own logs altered overnight — his handwriting describing events he never witnessed. The record itself is being rewritten. Beat: epistemological collapse.

chapters.title: Vane's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Vane, unraveling, reveals she was a student here in 1974 — the one who led the congregation downstairs and locked the door. Her authority was purchased with that act. Beat: power's original sin exposed.

chapters.title: The Well Refills
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Water rises in the undercroft; the school's taps run dark and singing. Two more students go missing in a single night. Beat: point of no return.

chapters.title: Descent Preparation
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral builds his kit: wax, rope, tape recorder running live, Imogen's notebook, and a written vow never to open his mouth below. Beat: grim resolve.

chapters.title: Last Day Above
chapters.summary: POV Coral. He mails his complete documentation to an outside address — insurance against erasure — and says goodbye to a school that no longer sees him. Beat: farewell to the ordinary world.

chapters.title: Through the Sealed Door
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The door opens willingly. Stairs descend into flooded dark; the harmonic becomes words. Coral descends recording everything. Beat: threshold crossed.

chapters.title: The Congregation
chapters.summary: POV Coral. He finds them: generations of the taken standing waist-deep in black water, faces inked-smooth, singing in perfect rounds. Imogen stands among them, half-changed. Beat: awe and horror fused.

chapters.title: The Song's Logic
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Listening, Coral understands: the song isn't a trap, it's a plea — the congregation sings to be finished, released, remembered. Finishing it wrongly would make him their conductor forever. Beat: moral complexity.

chapters.title: Vane Below
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Vane follows him down, confessing she comes every decade to renew the seal with a name. Tonight the name was meant to be Coral's. Beat: betrayal crystallized.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: POV Coral. At the chapel's heart lies the well itself, breathing like a throat. The torn final verse is carved on its rim — reading it counts as learning it. Beat: temptation at its purest.

chapters.title: Do Not Sing Along
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The choir turns to Coral and offers him the melody, sweet and inevitable. His jaw aches to join. He bites down on his own sleeve and listens instead. Beat: supreme restraint.

chapters.title: Learning by Ear
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Through three nights below, Coral transcribes the final verse onto paper, never voicing it, while the water climbs his chest. Beat: endurance as devotion.

chapters.title: Vane Sings
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Unable to bear the unfinished song, Vane sings the verse herself — and the well accepts her as its new keeper, dissolving her into harmony. Beat: power's wages paid.

chapters.title: The Well Breathes In
chapters.summary: POV Coral. With Vane taken, the well begins to refill ahead of schedule. Coral has minutes. He holds the completed verse and realizes the release requires a singer — just not a willing one. Beat: desperate insight.

chapters.title: The Unwilling Voice
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral plays back his own sleep-tapes at full volume into the well — his stolen second voice singing the verse he never spoke. The congregation stills. Beat: turning his violation into the weapon.

chapters.title: Release
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The song completes; the inked faces regain their features for one moment of recognition and gratitude before the water takes them gently down. Imogen surfaces, human, gasping. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Ascent
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral carries Imogen up as the undercroft floods behind them, sealing itself forever. His tape recorder dies at the top step, erasing everything below. Beat: exhausted deliverance.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Documented
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The school remembers nothing; registers show full attendance. Only Coral's mailed carbon copies preserve the truth — and they read strangely, as if someone else wrote them. Beat: hollow victory.

chapters.title: The Changed Children
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The returned students are quiet, watchful, and sometimes hum two bars they shouldn't know. Imogen thanks Coral without knowing why. Beat: unresolved tenderness.

chapters.title: Coral's Last Log
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral makes his final dictation, resigns, and burns his copy of the verse unread. For the first time since childhood, he speaks a full paragraph without stammering. Beat: identity reclaimed at cost.

chapters.title: New Post
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Months later, Coral takes a post at a coastal school. On his first night he hears, faintly, a harmonic under the tide — and chooses, deliberately, not to record it. Beat: hard-won wisdom.

chapters.title: Refill
chapters.summary: POV Coral, coda. An epistolary chapter: the outside archive receives one anonymous addition — a page in unfamiliar handwriting containing the song's final verse, and beneath it, freshly inked, a new face waiting to be blotted out. Beat: the cycle, patient, beginning again.
